A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same ReDDiT research. v2 includes supplementary Sections 6–9; v3 ends after the references and contains no corresponding appendix. This is an identifiable difference between the supplied documents, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v2 reports original enhancement results, acceleration comparisons, ablations, and efficiency measurements in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–10.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, acceleration comparisons, ablations, and efficiency measurements in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–8.

M1.justification: Trajectory distillation, reflectance-aware refinement, and pixel/perceptual auxiliary losses remain unchanged. Equations (5) and (7) express minimization of the existing objectives using argmin notation; they do not introduce a different training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain evaluations on LOLv1, LOLv2-real, LOLv2-synthetic, SID, SDSD, DICM, LIME, MEF, NPE, and VV. The omitted supplementary figures concern these existing benchmarks, so their removal does not establish reduced dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 omits Figure 9's SID/SDSD visual comparisons against Zero-DCE, EnGAN, and Retinexformer. It also loses Figure 10's additional unpaired visual comparisons against EnGAN, Zero-DCE, and GSAD. Comparator membership in the retained quantitative tables and acceleration comparison is unchanged.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same metrics, sampling-step comparisons, and stated transfer of the LOLv2-synthetic model to unpaired datasets. Supplementary split, preprocessing, and training specifications disappear, but no replacement settings or changed procedures are reported; this is a documentation loss under D1.

E4.justification: Figures 6–8 retain the same analyses of refinement-component choice, refinement strength, and auxiliary losses. The omitted supplementary figures provide benchmark comparisons without a distinct robustness or diagnostic analysis. Neither supplied PDF actually includes the promised single-step failure examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The supplementary iteration counts concern training budgets, not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the numerical trends in Figures 5–8 remain unchanged; for example, Ours-8 retains LOLv1 PSNR 28.090. v3 removes the SID/SDSD visual results in Figure 9 and the additional baseline outputs in Figure 10. Several unpaired images remain displayed in Figure 4.

T1.justification: v2 Section 6's explicit proof of Corollary 1, Equations (17)–(20), is absent from v3, although the corollary and main derivations remain. The argmin rewrites in Equations (5) and (7) restate the existing objectives rather than adding mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about fitting errors, the inference gap, RATR, comparable two-step performance, four/eight-step SOTA results, and validation on ten benchmarks. The new code-access sentence does not alter these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of residual-space refinement, increasing refinement importance at fewer steps, and PairLIE's shortcomings remain unchanged. Section 4.6 retains the single-step restoration and lightweight-network limitations. The omitted supplementary discussion largely repeats existing enhancement and generalization interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 removes the only detailed implementation and dataset specifications: the SR3 teacher setup, two-million/5,000 training/distillation iterations, optimizer, EMA, noise schedule, patch/batch sizes, A100 hardware, dataset splits, and RAW-to-sRGB processing. It adds a project-page code link, but the supplied PDF no longer documents these essential reproduction details.

R1.justification: v3 adds Vonikakis et al.'s 'On the evaluation of illumination compensation algorithms' as the VV citation and removes Saharia et al.'s SR3 reference with the supplementary implementation section. The related-work discussion and claim of the first distilled diffusion approach tailored to LLIE remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section ordering remain stable, with limited punctuation, capitalization, and typo corrections, updated author affiliations/contribution notes, and a code-access sentence. The supplementary block is omitted without a broader rewrite of the retained text.

P2.justification: Supplementary Figures 9–10 are removed; Figure 10 partly expanded the retained Figure 4 with additional comparator columns. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–4 preserve their displays, with small caption corrections and first-page/reference-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The decisive loss is the only detailed training, preprocessing, and dataset-split specification, substantially weakening reproducibility. v3 also omits Corollary 1's promised proof and supplementary visual evidence while retaining references to supplementary material. The new code-access pointer and editorial corrections offer benefits, but the supplied PDFs provide no replacement for the removed technical documentation.
